The invention provides a method and device for determining spatially dependent X-ray flux degradation and changes in the photon spectrum of an X-ray tube.

The device comprises an acquisition unit, a processing unit, a calculation unit, and a combination unit. The acquisition unit collects data relating to the degradation of the X-ray flux. The processing unit then converts the collected data into spatially dependent flux degradation data, thereby indicating how the reduction in X-ray flux varies across different spatial positions.

The calculation unit determines changes in the photon spectrum of the X-ray tube and converts these changes into a spatially dependent spectrum. This spectrum represents the variation in photon energy distribution as a function of spatial position.

Finally, the combination unit integrates the spatially dependent flux degradation data with the spatially dependent spectrum. The resulting combined information provides a comprehensive spatial characterization of both X-ray flux degradation and photon spectral changes for the X-ray tube.
outputs.L4:
A device, system, and method are provided for characterizing spatially dependent changes in the performance of an X-ray tube. During operation and aging, an X-ray tube may exhibit a reduction in photon flux as well as changes in the emitted photon-energy spectrum. These effects may vary with position, emission angle, detector location, or region within an imaging field. A spatially averaged measurement may therefore fail to identify localized degradation that can affect image quality, dose estimates, calibration accuracy, and system performance.

Degradation data are acquired at multiple spatial locations or for multiple X-ray beam paths. The data may be obtained using one or more detectors, repeated measurements at different detector positions, a detector array, or measurements collected while an X-ray source, detector, collimator, or other system component is moved. The acquired data can include photon counts, detector signals, energy-resolved measurements, attenuation measurements, operating parameters, or combinations thereof. Reference data associated with a new, calibrated, or previously characterized X-ray tube may also be stored for comparison.

A processor receives and analyzes the acquired degradation data. The analysis can include correcting detector response, normalizing measurements for tube current and exposure time, removing background signals, and comparing current measurements with corresponding reference measurements. From this analysis, the processor determines the reduction in X-ray flux at each sampled spatial location. Measurements between sampled locations may be interpolated or modeled to generate a spatially resolved flux-degradation map.

The processor also calculates changes in the photon-energy spectrum. Spectral changes may be determined directly from energy-resolving detector data or indirectly from measurements obtained through filters, attenuating materials, or other spectral discrimination components. The calculated changes can include shifts in effective energy, changes in spectral shape, variations in low- and high-energy photon content, or changes within selected energy intervals. These results are associated with the corresponding spatial coordinates to produce a spatially dependent representation of the tube spectrum.

The spatially dependent flux-degradation information is then combined with the spatially dependent spectral information. The combined characterization indicates not only where the X-ray output has decreased, but also how the energy distribution of the emitted radiation has changed at each location. Results may be presented as maps, tables, profiles, correction factors, or parameterized models and may be stored for monitoring changes over time.

The resulting information can be used to calibrate an imaging system, compensate acquired images, refine radiation-dose calculations, identify nonuniform tube wear, predict remaining tube life, or determine when maintenance or replacement is appropriate. By separately determining flux loss and spectral change and then combining those quantities on a spatially resolved basis, the device, system, and method provide a more complete and accurate assessment of X-ray tube performance than a single integrated or spatially averaged measurement.

### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. Saying “a book” could mean any book, while “the book” refers to one that is already known or clearly identified.

Although it often goes unnoticed, “the” helps make communication precise and natural. It connects speakers through shared understanding and gives context to everyday sentences. This simple three-letter word shows that even the smallest parts of language can have a significant impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a device and system that determine spatially dependent X-ray flux degradation and photon spectral changes in an X-ray tube.
counterfactuals.output: A device and system for determining spatially dependent degradation of X-ray flux and changes in photon spectra produced by an X-ray tube are disclosed. The system includes one or more energy-resolving X-ray detectors positioned to receive radiation emitted from respective spatial regions of an X-ray focal spot, anode, or beam field. A collimator, coded aperture, or movable sampling assembly selectively associates detected photons with the respective spatial regions. Processing circuitry obtains energy-dependent measurement data, corrects the data for detector response and acquisition geometry, and compares the corrected data with reference data or a tube model. The processing circuitry determines, for each spatial region, at least one of photon flux, spectral distribution, effective energy, filtration, or a degradation metric, and generates a spatial map representing temporal changes in tube output. The resulting information may be used to identify localized tube wear, predict tube life, provide maintenance notifications, or control operating parameters to compensate for spatially nonuniform flux or spectral degradation.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent-style abstract covering a device, system, method, computer program element, and computer-readable medium for analyzing spatial variations in X-ray tube flux degradation and photon spectra.
counterfactuals.output: A device, system, method, computer program element, and non-transitory computer-readable medium are provided for analyzing spatial variations in X-ray tube flux degradation and photon spectra. Measurement data representing X-ray emissions at a plurality of spatial locations within an irradiation field are acquired using one or more radiation detectors, optionally at multiple tube operating conditions, filtration states, or times. A processor spatially registers and normalizes the measurement data, compensates for detector response and acquisition geometry, and determines, for each spatial location, one or more flux-degradation parameters and spectral characteristics. The spectral characteristics may include photon-energy distributions, effective energy, filtration, half-value layer, spectral-shape parameters, or energy-bin intensities. Spatial degradation and spectral-variation maps are generated by comparison with baseline measurements, reference models, or previously acquired data. The processor may identify nonuniform degradation, distinguish temporal tube-output changes from anode, focal-spot, filtration, collimation, or detector effects, and estimate uncertainty or confidence values. The resulting maps and parameters may be used to generate alerts, predict tube condition, schedule maintenance, modify imaging protocols, or apply spatially dependent calibration or exposure corrections. The computer program element comprises instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause performance of the analysis, and the computer-readable medium stores the instructions.

**Abstract**

An invention for analyzing degradation of an X-ray tube is disclosed. A device (10) comprises an acquisition unit (11) configured to acquire operating data associated with operation of the X-ray tube; a processing unit (12) configured to process the operating data and derive one or more degradation-related parameters; a calculation unit (13) configured to calculate respective degradation indicators based on the parameters; and a combination unit (14) configured to combine the degradation indicators to determine a degradation state, failure risk, and/or remaining useful life of the X-ray tube. The operating data may include electrical, thermal, radiation-output, exposure-history, and environmental data. The invention further relates to an X-ray system comprising the device (10), a corresponding computer-implemented degradation-analysis method, software comprising instructions that cause a processor to perform the method, and a computer-readable storage medium storing the software.
